newsitem.title: FRANCE: French MATIF exchange jostles for "euro" prowess.
newsitem.headline: French MATIF exchange jostles for "euro" prowess.

text.p: France's MATIF financial futures and options exchange unveiled a "euro" strategy on Wednesday which it hopes will win it the battle for dominance between European markets with the advent of a single currency.

MATIF, Europe's second largest derivatives exchange, said in a statement one of the cornerstones of its strategy would be the creation of euro-denominated interest rate products with maturities right across the yield curve.
The French exchange, whose efforts to link up with Germany's Deutsche Boerse stock and options exchange collapsed in August, discussed strategy on Tuesday.
It said it also decided to adapt its 10-year bond futures contract to better align it with 10-year cash bonds.

It said the board supported efforts to develop alliances with partners in other time zones in America and in Asia to deal with a global market in euros that will come with the move to monetary union in 1999.
MATIF said it was also planning to cut the costs of access to the market and adapting current contracts in francs to get ready for the euro.
